{"summary":"Read-only product and release plan for MSW 3.1.0 on native macOS 26. Product boundary: ship a calm MenuBarExtra monitor and launcher for dev, playgrounds, and personal; keep msw as the policy boundary for every mutation; never start VMs while polling; distinguish stopped, transitioning, unavailable, stale, missing, and quarantined states; never display or log credentials; and never expose raw msb mutations by default.

Capability matrix and priority: (1) Installation/bootstrap — R1 detects Apple Silicon, msw/msb versions, configuration, host integration, and all three managed workspaces; it explains failures and opens an exact Ghostty command. setup.sh, Homebrew installation, sudo, base-snapshot rebuild, workspace recreation, config reset, and initial deep checks remain deliberate terminal workflows. (2) Lifecycle — R1 provides Start, Stop, and Restart for each workspace plus explicitly separated all-workspace actions, progress, cancellation-safe UI, per-workspace operation locks, readiness results, and quarantine enforcement. Start is a direct user action; Stop/Restart require confirmation; all-workspace operations receive a stronger confirmation. (3) Metrics/logs — R1 shows bounded CPU and memory snapshots with observed-at timestamps; R2 adds detailed charts and bounded, searchable, pausable JSON log streaming with copy and terminal handoff. Transport failures preserve the last good snapshot as stale and never become false Stopped states. (4) Repositories — R2 adds on-demand repository discovery, clone, fast-forward-only pull, per-repository results, and Zed/Ghostty launchers. The UI must disclose that repository discovery can start a stopped VM and validate every workspace-relative path. (5) Ports/tunnels — R1 provides configured URL construction, copy/open actions, and favorite ports; R2 adds a searchable published-port list and tracked tunnels with validated local/remote ports, visible process lifetime, URL, and Stop action. Published ports are labelled configured, not active. (6) GitHub authentication — R1 reports read-token presence, host-write availability, access mode, verification repository, verification age, and quarantine without revealing tokens. R2 supports explicit verification with progress and conflict locking. Token setup/removal remains terminal-first because the CLI owns hidden input, Keychain writes, secret binding, rollback, and quarantine behavior. (7) Host-only pushes — R3 adds a review sheet showing workspace, canonical repository, path, branch, exact SHA, remote state, commits, and fast-forward mode. It must invoke msw push, preserve typed PUSH confirmation, never add --yes, keep force-with-lease behind a separate advanced warning, and retain the guest-read/host-write credential split. (8) Disk/resources — R3 presents guest filesystem and Docker usage separately, warns that disk inspection starts stopped VMs, and offers bounded resize controls using the repository ceilings: dev 12 CPU/48 GB, playgrounds 12 CPU/48 GB, personal 12 CPU/32 GB, including aggregate host-pressure warnings. (9) Maintenance — R3 supports volume-preserving Docker cleanup after confirmation; deleting unused volumes requires typed confirmation. Guest upgrade, MicroSandbox update, host repair, setup repair flags, and arbitrary exec remain advanced terminal workflows until structured preview/progress contracts exist. (10) Backup/restore — R3 provides a backup wizard with destination, sensitive-archive warning, affected running set, progress, archive/checksum/info results, and verification that only previously running VMs restart. Restore remains a recovery workflow outside the popover: verify checksum and member safety, preview replacement scope, preserve typed RESTORE, retain rollback state, leave VMs stopped, and explain that Keychain tokens are unchanged. (11) Diagnostics — R1 includes version/config/CLI presence, quick check, copy-redacted diagnostics, retry, and terminal repair guidance. Deep check requires confirmation because it starts VMs and creates temporary services/containers; host repair stays terminal-visible because it uses sudo and modifies loopbacks, hosts, launch-daemon, and SSH state. (12) Settings — R1 stores only non-sensitive preferences: CLI path, polling cadence, port favorites, scheme, terminal/editor, launch at login, notification opt-in, backup destination, display choices, and update channel. No tokens or raw environments enter app preferences. (13) Updates — distribute a Developer ID-signed and notarized macOS 26 app through a signed update feed with phased rollout, compatibility checks, user-visible release notes, and rollback support. App updates, msw package installation, msw update of MicroSandbox, and msw upgrade of guest packages remain distinct; the app never silently runs the latter three. (14) Escape hatches — every unsupported or failed workflow offers an exact, copyable, argv-launched Ghostty command. The app never interpolates user input into a shell, embeds an arbitrary terminal, clears quarantine, or bypasses confirmations.

Automation policy: background automation is limited to read-only status/metrics/version checks, freshness handling, deduplicated opt-in notifications, and update availability. Safe explicit actions include Start, Refresh, Copy URL, Open URL/Zed/Ghostty, viewing docs, and stopping a tracked tunnel. Confirmation dialogs cover Stop/Restart, all-workspace lifecycle operations, clone/pull-all, GitHub verification, backup, resize, normal cleanup, and deep diagnostics. Typed confirmation is mandatory for PUSH, RESTORE, destructive volume cleanup, and any future native recreate/reset operation. GitHub token setup/removal, force-with-lease, setup repair flags, guest/host upgrades, host repair, arbitrary exec, and raw msb administration remain deliberate advanced workflows.

First shippable release: first stabilize versioned JSON contracts for status, metrics, GitHub status, repositories, and ports while preserving human CLI output. Then ship R1 with installation preflight, three fixed workspace cards, non-starting polling, metrics snapshots, Start/Stop/Restart, Refresh, URL/Zed/Ghostty launchers, GitHub health, quick diagnostics, activity/error history, stale-state semantics, settings, login item, opt-in notifications, terminal fallback, keyboard navigation, VoiceOver, and signed updating. This is coherent daily value without prematurely rebuilding sensitive CLI transactions.

Later phases: R2 adds streaming logs, repository discovery/clone/pull, the full ports view, tunnels, GitHub verification, and a detail window. R3 adds guarded push, disk/resource controls, backup, deep checks, resize, identity, and cleanup. R4 considers secure native recovery and maintenance flows only after structured preview/result APIs exist; terminal handoff remains permanently supported.

User stories: a developer can see the trustworthy state and freshness of all three isolated workspaces at a glance; start, stop, or restart exactly the intended workspace; inspect resource pressure without waking stopped VMs; open a site, repository, Zed session, or Ghostty shell quickly; find repositories and perform bounded clone/pull operations; understand configured ports and manage temporary tunnels; verify GitHub access without seeing tokens; review and explicitly authorize a host-only push; identify disk pressure and resize within policy; create a recoverable cold backup; restore only through a visibly guarded transaction; diagnose installation, quarantine, and connectivity failures; configure non-sensitive behavior; update the app independently; and escape to an exact CLI command whenever the GUI should not own the workflow.

Success criteria: 100% of commands exposed by msw help are classified as native, confirmed, typed-confirmation, or terminal-only; opening the app or leaving it idle for 24 hours starts zero stopped VMs; initial cached UI appears within one second and a fresh status result within three seconds on a healthy Mac; lifecycle UI acknowledges execution within one second and converges with CLI state within 15 seconds or shows a specific timeout; metrics refresh every 2–5 seconds only while visible and stop when hidden; stale data always includes its observation time; log memory is bounded and secret redaction tests pass; no token, Keychain value, command environment, or private repository content appears in diagnostics; all process launches use executable-plus-argv with no shell interpolation; conflicting workspace mutations cannot overlap; every destructive fake-path test proves the required phrase cannot be bypassed; backup tests prove checksum creation and previous-running-set restoration; restore tests prove pre-mutation validation, rollback, and stopped final state; all primary controls work with keyboard and VoiceOver; and signed update verification rejects altered packages.

Migration and measurable verification milestones: M0 records the current CLI behavior and trust invariants with no app dependency. M1 lands schema-versioned JSON fixtures and achieves complete command-inventory mapping plus parser rejection of unknown schemas. M2 read-only alpha demonstrates all three cards, zero polling-induced starts across a 24-hour soak, stale/offline/quarantine fixtures, and bounded resource usage. M3 release candidate exercises all nine per-workspace Start/Stop/Restart paths, all-workspace confirmations, launchers, quick diagnostics, accessibility, login item, notifications, signing/notarization, and update rollback. M4 daily-workflow release verifies logs, repositories, ports, tunnels, and GitHub verification against fakes plus a disposable real workspace. M5 guarded-operations release proves PUSH/RESTORE/destructive-clean phrases, force-with-lease separation, backup recovery, path containment, redaction, cancellation, and operation locking. M6 advanced flows are eligible for native UI only after machine-readable preview/result contracts and transactional failure tests exist.

Verification performed without tests, formatters, linters, or writes: reviewed README.md, config.sh, setup.sh, the complete bin/msw help/dispatcher and relevant safety implementations, documentation, named test coverage, and the existing planning artifact; confirmed the inventory includes installation and repair flags, all public msw commands, internal/non-command exclusions, repository-specific resource limits, credential quarantine, push confirmation, backup running-set behavior, restore validation/rollback, and terminal-only boundaries. No repository files were edited by this task.","filesChanged":[]}
